30303-the-passing-of-ku-sui:
Anthony Gilmore tells The Passing of Ku Sui, a complete novelette from Astounding Stories, November 1932. A table of contents added by the transcriber, and one word in chapter two marked as illegible, accompany it. Hawk Carse's career divides broadly into three main phases. This intimate narrative concerns the Ku Sui adventures of the second phase, which John Sewell, the historian, baldly condenses together from adventures of a century ago.

Research and closer scrutiny, Gilmore notes, give those adventures an individuality and significance deserving separate treatment. The plan, three figures in the dawn, a raid, the voice of the brains, congratulations to Captain Carse, and a deadline follow. To the laboratory, White's brain and Yellow's head, four bodies, a promise fulfilled, an ordeal, a flight, Earth's shadow, the Hawk striking, and a meteor follow. An illustration shows Hawk Carse shooting like a projectile away from Earth.
30409-a-short-essay-toward-the-improveme:
Isaac Watts writes A Short Essay Toward the Improvement of Psalmody, first printed at the end of his 1707 Hymns and Spiritual Songs and omitted from the 1818 reprint. This text keeps the original 1707 page numbers, spelling, punctuation, and even errors, with the long s modernized and broken words rejoined.

Watts asks how psalmody should fit the gospel state, what songs to leave out, and how singing should be managed under the gospel. He draws on scripture songs and on writers such as Dr. Patrick, seeking beauty and fitness in worship. The essay remains a key early argument for richer, more evangelical congregational song.
9939-woman-s-institute-library-of-cooker:
Volume five of the Woman's Institute cookery course turns to fruit and its keeping: fruit desserts, canning and drying, jelly making, preserving, and pickling, with confections, beverages, and the planning of meals. It opens with fruit in the diet and the food value of fruits.

Later sections teach how to can, dry, and pickle safely, how to set jellies, and how to plan balanced meals around the seasons. The lessons suit a time when fruit was growing less seasonal but still needed care. Home cooks get the skills for preserving summer's plenty for winter tables.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acqui:
Acqui is a diocese suffragan of Turin in Italy, holding ninety-three towns in Alexandria province, twenty-three in Genoa, and one in Cuneo. Its first indubitable bishop is Ditarius, whose tablet, found in 1753 in St. Peter's church, records his death on 25 January 488. Popular tradition names earlier bishops, earliest Majorinus, who probably lived at the end of the fourth or start of the fifth century.

The diocese likely arose at the fourth century's end, at the same time as Novara, Turin, Ivrea, and Aosta. The entry argues that the seven years of Honorius, 395 to 402, offered the best time for such foundations. Northern Italy and southern Gaul were then reorganized, after agreement between church and emperors. Sources include Gams, Brady, Lanigan, and local histories of Acqui.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-fray-jose-arl:
José Arlegui, a Spaniard from Biscay, moved from the Franciscan province of Cantabria to Zacatecas in Mexico. There he wrote on theology and on the native peoples. His best-known book, the Chronicle of Zacatecas, appeared in 1737. It remains the main source for a region few other published works touch. The entry sketches a working friar whose writing doubled as early ethnology.

Inside the chronicle, Arlegui recounts the missions of his province. He gathers many facts about its native inhabitants and their first contacts with Christianity. Readers who want the early history of Zacatecas still lean on his pages. Nearly everything known about those peoples and missions comes through this one friar's work.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-juan-de-jaure:
Juan de Jáuregui was a Spanish painter and poet of Seville's golden age. Born about 1570, a knight of Calatrava, he studied the old masters in Rome and won fame as a portrait painter, perhaps painting Cervantes himself. As a poet he began as a disciple of Herrera, sometimes following his model too closely.

Jáuregui's blank-verse version of Tasso's Aminta, first printed in Italy in 1607, ranks among the best foreign renderings of that pastoral play. He first attacked Gongorism's obscure style, then fell under its spell in his Orfeo of 1624 and even defended it. His complete Pharsalia of Lucan appeared only in 1684, after his death about 1640.

podcast-dannyjones-X9ShiRDhvUI:
John Vervaeke joins Danny Jones for a wide talk on God, religion, and what happens when we die. The title also names ghosts in the brain, a nod to how the mind shapes what we see and feel. Vervaeke is a scholar who studies wisdom and the mind.

The two work through big questions about faith, the brain, and the sense that life has deep meaning. Vervaeke draws on science and old wisdom in the same breath. Jones presses him on death and on why the hunger for meaning will not go away. Listeners get a calm, deep talk on the largest questions a person can ask.
podcast-tuckercarlson-leY9FUqk1uI:
Host Tucker Carlson talks with Clayton Morris, a former television host who now runs an independent media show. Their subject is a Trump-backed ceasefire and the business of war coverage. Morris brings a skeptical view of large news firms.

Together they argue that major outlets gain money and reach from long wars. They question how ceasefire news gets framed for viewers at home. The transcript sample for the episode is badly garbled, so the title states the theme most clearly. Listeners get an anti-war, media-critical take from two allied voices.
podcast-tuckercarlson-yB05HiKCCuI:
Podcaster and veteran Shawn Ryan joins Tucker Carlson for a talk that roams from Trump to demons. The title names Trump's betrayal, Iran, state spying, and Ryan's road to God. Ryan hosts a hit show of his own with veterans and spies.

Ryan tells why he feels let down by Trump and where he thinks the country is led astray. He shares tales of dark forces he says he met in his own life. Carlson draws out his turn to faith. Listeners get two of the right's big voices in a frank talk. The library keeps it as a record of their chat.
woman-s-institute-library-of-cookery-vol: Volume Five of the Woman's Institute Library of Cookery covers fruit, canning, jelly making, sweets, drinks, and meal planning. Pages present here hold a contents list, but no recipes or lessons. The fruit section lists berries first, then apples, peaches, pears, and citrus fruits. Each fruit gets notes on food value and serving. Later sections named in the volume plan cover drying, preserving, pickling, and confections.
